# 2nd Experiment: VSFactors
The effect on the posterior inclusion probabilities (PIP) of increasing the number of levels within factors.
```{r Options}
metodo <- "GibbsBVS" # GibbsBVS, deterministic
machine <- "server" # server, local
master_seed <- 1234
n_workers <- 20

num_iter <- 10 # Number of replicates for each scenario
num_factors <- 4
n  <- 300 # Sample size
n1 <- 30  # No. of obs assigned to the 1st level of the active factor
alpha <- 1 # Intercept
beta11_vec <- c(0.7, 0.55) # Other values can also be tested

levs <- list(
  l5 = 5,
  l15 = 15
)

mp2 <- list(
  SBC = BAS:::SBC(),
  SBSB = BAS:::SBSB()
)

# Cartesian Product (df)
scenarios2 <- expand.grid(
  lev_name = names(levs),
  beta_id  = seq_along(beta11_vec),
  iter = seq_len(num_iter)
)
```

```{r Priors on Model Parameters}
priors_on_beta <- list(
  robust       = BAS::robust(n = n)#,
  #intrinsic    = BAS::intrinsic(n = n),
  #beta_prime   = BAS::beta.prime(n = n),
  #CH_a05_bn    = BAS::CCH(alpha = 1/2, beta = n),
  #CH_a1_bn     = BAS::CCH(alpha = 1, beta = n),
  #CH_a05_b05n  = BAS::CCH(alpha = 1/2, beta = n/2),
  #CH_a1_b05n   = BAS::CCH(alpha = 1, beta = n/2),
  # unit_inf_DBF = BAS::g.prior(g = n), # Unit information Prior (data-based Bayes Factors)
  # unit_inf_TBF = BAS::testBF.prior(g = n), # Unit information Prior (test-based Bayes Factors)
  #ZS_adapted   = BAS::CCH(alpha = 1, beta = 2, s = n + 3),
  #benchmark    = BAS::CCH(alpha = 0.02, beta = 0.02 * max(n, p^2)), # need to define p before this if used; with the recommended c = 0.01;
  #hyper_gn     = BAS::hyper.g.n(alpha = 3), # special case of the robust prior...
  #BIC          = BAS::bic.prior(n), # favors small models
	#AIC          = BAS::aic.prior(), # favours large models
  #local_eb     = BAS::EB.local(), # tends to favor large models
)
```

```{r Simulated Data Parallel}
library(future.apply)
library(dplyr)

generate_data <- function (scenarios = scenarios2) {

  future_lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(scenarios)),
  function(i) {

    lev_name <- as.character (scenarios$lev_name[i])
    l <- levs[[lev_name]]

    j <- scenarios$beta_id[i]
    beta11 <- beta11_vec[j]
  
    factors <- vector("list", num_factors)

    if (l == 2) {
      factors[[1]] <- c(rep(1, n1), rep (2, n - n1))
    } else {
      factors[[1]] <- c(rep(1, n1), sample(2:l, n - n1, replace = TRUE))
    }
    if (num_factors > 1) {
      for (j in 2:num_factors) {
        factors[[j]] <- sample(1:l, n, replace = TRUE)
      }
    }
    
    # Design matrix 
    X <- do.call(cbind, factors)
    # Overparameterized design matriz
    X_over <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = num_factors * l);
    # One-hot encoding
    for (k in seq_len(ncol(X))) {
      X_over[cbind(1:n, (k - 1) * l + X[, k])] <- 1
    }
    
    beta  <- c(
      beta11, rep (0, l - 1),  # 1st Factor (only the 1st level is active)
      rep (0, (ncol(X)-1) * l) # Spurious Factors
    )    

    eta <- alpha + X_over %*% beta # Linear predictor
    y <- rpois(n, lambda = exp (eta))

    sim_data <- as.data.frame(X) |>
      setNames(paste0("F", seq_len(ncol(X)))) |> # colNames
      dplyr::mutate(dplyr :: across(
        everything(),
        ~ relevel(factor(.x, levels = seq_len(l)), ref = "2")
        # as.factor
      )) |>
      dplyr::mutate(y = y, .before = 1) # 1st column: y
    
  },
  future.seed = TRUE
  )

}
```

```{r Build Formula Function}
build_formula <- function (p) {
  vars <- paste0("F", seq_len(p))
  formula <- as.formula(
    paste("y ~", paste(vars, collapse = " + "))
  )
  return(formula)
}
```

```{r Run bas_glmFC deterministic}
run_deterministic2 <- function(prior_name, data_i, beta_name) {
  
  obj <- BAS::bas.glmFC(
    formula = build_formula(num_factors),
    family = poisson(link = "log"),
    data = data_i,
    betaprior = priors_on_beta [[beta_name]],
    modelprior = mp2[[prior_name]],
    method = "deterministic",
    laplace = FALSE, # set to true for CCH and beta-prime 
    store_less = TRUE # TRUE, FALSE
  )
  return(obj$pip)
}
```

```{r Run bas_glmFC GibbsBVS}
run_gibbs2 <- function(prior_name, data_i, lev_name, beta_name) {

  l <- levs[[lev_name]]

  # Initial Model: NULL (default), Random Model: c(1,rbinom(n = (num_factors*l), size = 1, prob = .5)), Full Model: rep(1, (num_factors*l) + 1)
  init_model <- c(1, rbinom(n = (num_factors * l), size = 1, prob = .5))

  obj <- BAS::bas.glmFC(
    formula = build_formula(num_factors),
    family = poisson(link = "log"),
    data = data_i,
    betaprior = priors_on_beta [[beta_name]],
    modelprior = mp2[[prior_name]],
    method = "GibbsBVS",
    bestmodel = init_model,
    burnin.iterations = 5000, 
    MCMC.iterations = 50000, 
    laplace = FALSE, # set to true for CCH and beta-prime
    renormalize = FALSE, # PIPs are the MCMC relative frequencies of inclusion
    GROW = TRUE,
    expand = 1.25,
    n.models.init = 5000 # 10000
  )
  return(obj$pip.MCMC)
}
```

```{r Results function}
library(future.apply)

sim_results2 <- function (scenarios, m_p, b_p, parallel = TRUE, workers = NULL) {

  # 'scenarios' now carries the replicate index (iter), so each row is one
  # independent run: all (lev_name, beta_id, iter) runs go out in a single batch

  # A single plan for the whole call, instead of starting and tearing down one
  # worker pool per stage (data generation) and per replicate
  if (parallel) {
    if (is.null(workers)) {
      workers <- min (nrow(scenarios), n_workers, parallelly::availableCores())
    }
    # multisession, deliberately, not multicore: a fork inherits an already
    # multi-threaded BLAS, and workers end up fighting over cores.
    plan (multisession, workers = workers)
    on.exit(plan (sequential), add = TRUE)
    message ("sim_results2 using ", future::nbrOfWorkers(), " workers for ",
             nrow(scenarios), " runs")
  } else {
    plan (sequential)
  }

  set.seed (master_seed)
  
  SIMUL_data <- generate_data (scenarios)

  run_one <- function (i) {
    if (metodo == "deterministic") {
      return (
        run_deterministic2 (
          prior_name = m_p,
          data_i = SIMUL_data[[i]], # dataset corresponding to scenarios i-th row
          beta_name = b_p
        )
      )
    } else if (metodo == "GibbsBVS") {
      return (
        run_gibbs2 (
          prior_name = m_p,
          data_i = SIMUL_data[[i]], # dataset corresponding to scenarios i-th row
          lev_name = as.character (scenarios$lev_name[i]),
          beta_name = b_p
        )
      )
    }
  }

  mat_list <- future_lapply (
    X = seq_len(nrow(scenarios)),
    FUN = run_one,
    future.seed = TRUE
  )

  mat.pip <- mat_list %>%
    do.call (rbind, .) %>%  # Converting into a matrix
    round(2)

  colnames (mat.pip) <- paste0("F", seq_len(ncol(mat.pip)))
    
  return(mat.pip)
  
}
```

```{r Aggregate Function}
agg_results <- function (m_p, b_p = "robust", parallel = TRUE, workers = NULL) {

  # No loop over replicates: they are rows of scenarios2 now, so the whole grid
  # is fitted in one parallel batch
  message ("--- ", m_p, ": ", nrow(scenarios2), " runs (",
           length(unique(scenarios2$iter)), " replicates) ---")

  mat.pip <- sim_results2 (
    scenarios2,
    m_p,
    b_p,
    parallel = parallel, workers = workers
  ) # dim: (nrow(scenarios2) x num_factors)

  # A "scenario" is everything except the replicate index; the reduction below
  # runs over iter, so these are the rows that survive into the output
  base_cols <- setdiff (names(scenarios2), "iter")
  scen_base <- unique (scenarios2[base_cols])
  rownames (scen_base) <- NULL

  # Row of scenarios2 (and hence of mat.pip) -> row of scen_base
  grp <- match (
    do.call (paste, c(scenarios2[base_cols], sep = "\r")),
    do.call (paste, c(scen_base[base_cols], sep = "\r"))
  )

  iters  <- sort (unique(scenarios2$iter))
  n_scen <- nrow (scen_base)
  p      <- ncol (mat.pip)

  # Stack the replicates along a 3rd margin, as before:
  # arr has dim (n_scen x num_factors x num_iter)
  arr <- array (
    NA_real_,
    dim = c(n_scen, p, length(iters)),
    dimnames = list (NULL, colnames(mat.pip), paste0("iter", iters))
  )
  for (s in seq_len(n_scen)) {
    rows <- which (grp == s)                          # one row per replicate
    rows <- rows[order (scenarios2$iter[rows])]       # ordered by iter
    arr[s, , ] <- t (mat.pip[rows, , drop = FALSE])
  }

  # apply over margins c(1, 2) => the reduction runs over the replicates only,
  # entry by entry, so the result keeps the (n_scen x num_factors) shape
  mat_pip <- apply (arr, c(1, 2), mean)                    # spurious factors
  # mat_pip[, 1] <- apply (arr[, 1, , drop = FALSE], 1, min) # active factor
  # drop = FALSE keeps arr[, 1, ] as an array when num_iter == 1
  colnames (mat_pip) <- paste0("F", seq_len(ncol(mat_pip)))
  # scen_base drops the iter column, so the output keeps the same shape and
  # columns as before (one row per lev_name x beta_id combination)
  mat_pip <- cbind (as.data.frame(mat_pip), scen_base)
  mat_pip$m_p <- m_p
  # Raw replicates kept for diagnostics: a list of length num_iter, each element
  # a matrix of size (n_scen x num_factors)
  attr(mat_pip, "replicates") <- lapply (seq_along(iters), function (j) {
    matrix (
      arr[, , j], nrow = n_scen, ncol = p,
      dimnames = list (NULL, colnames(mat_pip)[seq_len(p)])
    )
  })
  return (mat_pip)

}
```

```{r Aggregate Results}
system.time({
  exp2_SBC <- agg_results ("SBC", "robust", # robust, unit_inf_DBF, unit_inf_TBF
                           parallel = TRUE, workers  = n_workers)
})
print(exp2_SBC)
# reps_SBC <- attr(exp2_SBC, "replicates")
# reps_SBC[[1]]          # first replicate: n_scen x num_factors matrix
# length(reps_SBC)       # == num_iter

system.time({
  exp2_SBSB <- agg_results ("SBSB", "robust", parallel = TRUE, workers = n_workers)
})
print(exp2_SBSB)
# reps_SBSB <- attr(exp2_SBSB, "replicates")
# reps_SBSB[[1]]          # first replicate: n_scen x num_factors matrix
# length(reps_SBSB)       # == num_iter

exp2 <- rbind(exp2_SBC, exp2_SBSB)
print(exp2)
```

## Analysis of results and plots
```{r df Transformations}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

exp2_wide <- exp2 %>% # Size df: (nrow (exp) x 7)
  pivot_longer( # Stacking F1–F4 into 2 columns (names and values)
    cols = starts_with("F"),
    names_to = "Factor",
    values_to = "PIP"
  ) %>% # Size df: ((nrow(exp) * 4) x 5)
  unite(
    col = "model_lev", # New column name
    m_p, lev_name,
    sep = "_" # for combining the values of these 2 columns
  ) %>% # Size df: ((nrow(exp) * 4) x 4)
  pivot_wider ( # model_lev and PIP columns are dropped
    names_from = model_lev, # New column names
    values_from = PIP
  ) %>% # Size df: ((lenghth(beta11_vec) * 4) x (2 + (length(mp2)*length(levs)))
  dplyr :: select (# Ordering columns
    beta_id, Factor,
    starts_with("SBSB"),
    starts_with("SBC")) %>% 
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r Table Function, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
LaTex_table <- function (df, id) {
  
  df <- df %>% 
    dplyr :: filter (beta_id == id) %>% # subsetting the df 
    dplyr :: select (-c(beta_id, Factor))
  
  rownames (df) <- paste0("pip(F", seq_len(nrow(df)), "):")
  
  # keep only lx...ly
  colnames(df) <- sub("^[^_]+_", "", colnames(df))
  # l=x...l=y
  colnames(df) <- sub("^l([0-9]+)$", "l=\\1", colnames(df))

  header1 <- c (rep("SBSB", (ncol(df)/2)), rep("SBC", (ncol(df)/2)))
  
  out_df <- rbind (header1, colnames(df), df)
  rownames(out_df) <- c("Model Prior","Number levels", rownames(df))
  colnames(out_df) <- c(rep("",ncol(out_df)))

  return(out_df)

}
```

```{r Print Tables}
for (i in seq_along(beta11_vec)) {

  title <- paste0("β_{11} = ", beta11_vec[i])
  cat(title, "\n")
  
  out_df <- LaTex_table (exp2_wide, i)
  print (out_df, digits = 2)
  cat("\n")

}
```
